back_blocks.md: A **unified atomic mass unit** is defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. Its symbol is *u* (or Da, Dalton), and 1 *u* = 1.66 x 10<sup>-27</sup> kg.

cards.back_md: A **unified atomic mass unit** is defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. Its symbol is *u* (or Da, Dalton), and 1 *u* = 1.66 x 10<sup>-27</sup> kg.

front_blocks.md: How is the relative atomic mass (*A*<sub>r</sub>) of an element calculated from its isotopes?

back_blocks.md: Multiply each isotope's **mass number** by its **percentage abundance**, sum the results, then divide by 100. This gives the weighted average of the isotope masses.

front_blocks.md: Relative atomic mass has units of grams.

back_blocks.md: Relative atomic mass is a ratio (mass of one atom relative to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom), so the units cancel and it is dimensionless.

Relative atomic mass has units of grams.
cards.back_md:

front_blocks.md: The relative atomic mass (*A*<sub>r</sub>) is the ratio of the average mass of atoms of an element to the **..........**, defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a **..........**  atom.

back_blocks.md: The relative atomic mass (*A*<sub>r</sub>) is the ratio of the average mass of atoms of an element to the **unified atomic mass unit**, defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a **carbon-12** atom.

back_blocks.md: **Relative isotopic mass** is the mass of one atom of a specific isotope compared to the value of the unified atomic mass unit.

front_blocks.md: What is the relative molecular mass (*M*<sub>r</sub>) of water (H<sub>2</sub>O)? (A<sub>r</sub>: H = 1.0, O = 16.0)

back_blocks.md: *M*<sub>r</sub> = (2 x 1.0) + (1 x 16.0) = **18.0**. It is calculated by summing the relative atomic masses of all atoms in one molecule.

front_blocks.md: Isotopes of an element have the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.

back_blocks.md: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, giving them different mass numbers.
